title: Actual source constant-field restriction and pointwise power transport
statement: Let $k_0,k_1$ be finite fields, let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in both, and let $X/k_0,Y/k_1$ be schemes. A geometric-fiber isomorphism $\theta:\bar X\simeq\bar Y$ intertwining $F_{\bar Y}$ with $F_{\bar X}^r$ defines the source functor $R(F)=\theta_*(F,\phi^{[r]})$ on constructible pro-etale Weil sheaves [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. It is the restriction of the explicit pro-etale transport, preserves lissity [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves], and, for locally finite-type bases, preserves finite limits and colimits. For a morphism $c:Y\to X$, define pointwise power transport to mean that every finite point $z$ admits a finite point $x=c(z)$ and $e>0$ with $q_z=q_x^e$ and, for every constructible $F$, an equivalence of Frobenius modules $(F_x,F_x^e)\simeq(RF)_z$ [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. This property implies preservation of reality [def-wf-iota-real]. For an actual cartesian finite-field extension square, choose the canonical geometric-fiber isomorphism and take $r$ satisfying $\#k_1=(\#k_0)^r$.
